slides.label: Founder story · Nithin Kamath
slides.deck: Nithin Kamath started Zerodha in 2010 with *no outside investors*, and it pioneered discount broking in India.

slides.credit: Photo: unknown author (Pxhere) / Wikimedia Commons, CC0
slides.label: Before Zerodha
slides.deck: He began trading stocks in the late 1990s. After the dotcom bust, he worked at a call centre to fund it.

cards.v: “I spent four years at a call center, making unsolicited calls to people in the US.”

slides.credit: NSE, Mumbai · Photo: Ganesh Dhamodkar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
slides.label: 15 August 2010
slides.deck: It ran on NSE NOW, the exchange's free trading platform, and NSE waived its *~₹5 lakh* membership fee.

cards.s: Flat per order, or 0.03% if lower

slides.credit: Bengaluru · Photo: Saad Faruque / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
slides.deck: Zerodha says it handles *over 15%* of Indian retail trading volumes.

slides.credit: BSE, Mumbai · Photo: Niyantha Shekhar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
slides.label: The lesson
slides.deck: “If it takes more than two sentences to explain how a product makes money and where the risk sits, you should probably stay away.”
slides.cta: Nithin Kamath, on his blog, 14 Sep 2026
